title: System Fair Persistent Identity

permissions.reason: All TOBB routes use the existing DB-backed Super Admin flag; audit-only action codes are declared separately and are not route permissions.
No assignable permission is introduced; the existing Super Admin guard is authoritative and audit-only codes are on the TOBB audit contract.

menu.reason: No navigation item is added or retargeted.

route_guard.reason: The fairs route guard is unchanged.

notes: ADR-038 and ADR-040: preserve persistent fair ids, names, tenant relationships and scraper settings. Exact/whole-word identity plus city matching; ambiguous names/cities/editions require durable Super Admin review, remembered and correctable mappings. Expiry lock is stored end_date < Istanbul today, including after manual selection. Dates apply/keep as a pair; independent organizer/venue/website decisions, no blank clearing, optimistic review versions plus row locks, rejected identical suggestions suppressed until source/baseline changes. Manual sync only fetches a preview before explicit Apply; source/catalog digests reject stale previews. Reuse detached executor, scraper_run_history/log, cooperative cancellation/stale heartbeat policy and existing systemd scheduling pattern; one globally active system TOBB run, org NULL, Monday 03:00 Istanbul, no catch-up, current/next years, bounded independent year retries/partial results. Fairs-page shared tables/filter/control/dirty primitives expose review, selected-date bulk actions, preview, run history and mapping corrections alongside existing duplicate merge. Core existing notifications module owns in-app persistence and SA inbox; public HTTP and a purpose-separated worker notification credential, never a persisted user JWT. New audit action codes are system-scoped, not role-assignable. SaaS impact: system/tenant isolation, Core ownership, auth, job concurrency/retry/cancel/audit, secret boundary, migrations and real UI/runtime evidence required. No billing/entitlement/quota/org lifecycle/tenant deletion changes. GitHub PR/CI/merge requires strict-green verification; production deployment is outside this delivery.
